intendedUse: See INTENDED-USE.md. Requirements are what the recipe claims the ledger evidences. Each is satisfied by a contract type or an engine rule, and proven by the assertions a site's scripted OQ makes against its own install (OQ-PQ.md). build-matrix.py turns this file into TRACEABILITY.md.

requirements.text: A complaint investigation is opened by a named QA investigator as the accountable principal, with the orchestrating automation's consent recorded on the chain before any work.
requirements.satisfiedBy: calder-complaint-case-v1, principal gate; the propose, accept, activate handshake
oqAsserts: QA opens the case as principal and the record is created
the orchestrator's accept lands on the chain before activation
the case reads ACTIVE

requirements.text: Each dataset read is performed and signed by the automation that read it, under the case, with the source system declared before the read.
requirements.satisfiedBy: calder-evidence-read-v1 as a delegated child: performer is the reader, parentRecordId is the case, sourceSystem is in criteria
oqAsserts: the orchestrator delegates each read as a child with autoActivate
each child reads ACTIVE with the orchestrator as its principal and the reader as its performer

requirements.text: A read that issued any write to a system of record cannot stand as evidence, and a case containing one cannot close as read-only.
requirements.satisfiedBy: the read-only-invariant expression rule (evidence.mutating == false) plus cascade rollup on a one-shot child
oqAsserts: a read completion with mutating true settles FAILED
the case is held by rollup after a mutating one-shot read
QA accept is refused 422 on the rolled-up failure
the QA reject verdict lands and the case reads FAILED

requirements.text: The case cannot be closed while any read is still open; the close-out is admitted only once every read is terminal.
oqAsserts: the case completion is refused 422 while reads are open
the refusal names the open children
the case completion is admitted once every read is terminal

requirements.text: The close-out carries the 211.198(b) decisions with their conditional fields: investigation performed or a written reason naming the responsible person, CAPA reference when CAPA is required, report type and due date when reportable.
oqAsserts: a close-out with capaRequired true and no capaRef is refused
a close-out with reportable true and no reportType or reportDueBy is refused
a close-out with no investigation and no written reason is refused (211.198(b)(3))

requirements.text: The close-out binds the source records' write stamps so an auditor can show nothing was written between read and close.
requirements.satisfiedBy: sorWriteStampDigest on the close-out over the sourceRecords of every read; re-derived from the reads' evidence as a cross-record check
oqAsserts: the digest on the close-out equals the digest re-derived from the stamps the reads listed
the close-out's evidenceRecordIds equals the set of the case's read children
a stamp moved between read and close changes the re-derived digest

requirements.text: The QA close-out is a signature with meaning, linked to the completion it approves, by a named signer at a server time.
requirements.satisfiedBy: the principal verdict's checks object (signatureMeaning, signerName, signerRole, regulation, signedAt) preserved on the OUTCOME_REPORTED entry of the audit export
oqAsserts: QA accept with a signature meaning settles the case FULFILLED
the audit export's OUTCOME_REPORTED entry carries the signature meaning verbatim and names the completion it signs
the entry's reporter is the QA investigator's identity, not an org admin's

requirements.text: An automation's proposal to manufacture is notarized under its own identity, labelled by what produced it, before any check runs.
oqAsserts: the proposer notarizes the proposal and it reads RECORDED
a proposal with producedBy.kind llm and no model is refused

requirements.text: The release is opened by a named QA person from the control plan in the quality system, with the required checks and the plan's hash bound to the record.
oqAsserts: QA opens the release as principal with the control plan bound
the proposer's accept lands on the chain before activation
a release with empty requiredChecks is refused

requirements.text: The precondition check is performed by a deterministic checker, delegated under the release, carrying only the control plan hash copied from the release; the checker reads the plan from the quality system.
requirements.satisfiedBy: calder-precondition-check-v1 as a delegated child: performer is the checker, criteria carries controlPlanHash and no list
oqAsserts: the proposer delegates the check to the checker as a child
a check child whose criteria carries a list of checks is refused at create
a check child whose performer is the proposer itself is caught by the cross-record check (the engine admits it)
the child's controlPlanRef and controlPlanHash equal the release's (cross-record check)

requirements.text: No release completion can be submitted while the check child is open, and none while a failed check holds the release; the engine does not require the child to exist, so the release completion's checkRef is confirmed to name a FULFILLED child of the release.
requirements.satisfiedBy: engine cascade settlement: has_children_leaf_only, and failure rollup on a one-shot child; checkRef confirmed by QA or the cross-record check
oqAsserts: the release completion is refused 422 while the check is open
the release completion is still refused after a failed check
a release completed with no check child, or with a check child cancelled before work, is caught by the cross-record check (the engine admits it)
the release completion's checkRef names a FULFILLED child of the release (cross-record check)

requirements.text: The check settles FULFILLED only when every check the plan names passed, with the same names and count, against the same control plan hash; any failed, missing, renamed or extra check, or a stale plan, settles FAILED.
requirements.satisfiedBy: the all-required-checks-passed expression rule (evidence against evidence, plan hash against criteria)
oqAsserts: a short passed list (fewer than the plan names) settles FAILED
the same count with one check renamed settles FAILED
a stale control plan hash settles FAILED
one failed check settles FAILED
every required check passed settles FULFILLED

requirements.text: A failed check holds the release; QA can only reject it, nothing is written to the system of record, and a revision requested after the reject is visible on the chain.
requirements.satisfiedBy: cascade rollup (reject-only verdict) plus a system-of-record assertion
oqAsserts: the release is held by rollup after the failed one-shot check
QA accept is refused 422 on the rolled-up failure
the QA reject verdict lands and the release reads FAILED
no manufacturing order or lot exists in the system of record for the proposed lot
a revision requested on the rejected release appears on its chain

requirements.text: The release completion claims a fulfilled check by structure and binds the exact payload to be written by hash.
requirements.satisfiedBy: checkOutcome const FULFILLED; payloadHash sha256 pattern
oqAsserts: the release completion is admitted once the check is FULFILLED, with the payload hash bound
a release completion with checkOutcome FAILED is refused
a release completion without payloadHash is refused
a receipt without payloadHash is refused

requirements.text: The QA release approval is a signature with meaning (21 CFR 11.50) linked to the completion it signs (11.70), rendered by the record's principal.
requirements.satisfiedBy: the principal verdict's checks object preserved on the OUTCOME_REPORTED entry
oqAsserts: QA accept with a Part 11 signature meaning settles the release FULFILLED
the audit export's OUTCOME_REPORTED entry carries the signature meaning and names the completion it signs
the entry's reporter is the QA release signer's identity, not an org admin's

requirements.text: What was written to the system of record is notarized by the writer with the system's own id and write stamp, and its payload hash equals the hash QA approved.
requirements.satisfiedBy: calder-sor-write-receipt-v1; the receipt's payloadHash compared to the release completion's as a cross-record check
oqAsserts: the writer notarizes the receipt and it reads RECORDED, with the same payload hash as the release completion
the manufacturing order exists in the system of record with the approved lot
a receipt whose releaseRef is not a UUID is refused

requirements.text: Only the parent's performer can delegate a child, and no ancestor principal can be named as a child's performer.
oqAsserts: an agent that is not the release's performer cannot create the check child (binding of duty)
the release's principal (QA) cannot be named the checker (circular delegation)

requirements.text: Every record's chain verifies offline against out-of-band keys with the published verifier, and a corrupted chain is detected.
requirements.satisfiedBy: GET /v1/records/{id}/audit-export verified with agledger-verify against GET /v1/verification-keys
oqAsserts: every record's audit export verifies against the Server's verification keys
an export with one altered byte is reported as invalid
